[About my work]{.eyebrow}

## Understanding the citizen’s perspective

I am a Research Professor at NORCE and a Professor at the Department of Government, University of Bergen. I also coordinate the European Social Survey in Norway.

My work examines democratic legitimacy, political behaviour, and public opinion. I use survey experiments, deliberative polls, and other quantitative methods to understand how citizens respond to decision-making procedures, political outcomes, and new technologies.
:::

::: {.research-grid}
::: {.research-topic}
[01]{.topic-number}

### Democratic legitimacy

What makes a decision acceptable—including to the people who disagree with its outcome? I study representation, referendums, procedural fairness, and political loss.

[Democracy and legitimacy →](research.qmd#democratic-legitimacy)
:::

::: {.research-topic}
[02]{.topic-number}

### AI and public decisions

How does the use of AI change citizens’ views of government? My research examines fairness, acceptance, and the relationship between citizens and public employees.

[AI and governance →](research.qmd#ai-and-governance)
:::

::: {.research-topic}
[03]{.topic-number}

### Public opinion and participation

How are opinions formed, measured, and changed? My work includes survey methodology, deliberation, political participation, and election forecasting.

[Opinion and participation →](research.qmd#public-opinion-and-participation)
:::
:::
